# Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 -- Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-12

This log records all verses in Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 where the three translators significantly diverged.

---

## 5:1 — "Guard your foot" vs. "Guard your steps" vs. "keep your ears open"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Guard your-foot [raglekha]" | Literal singular |
| LOGOS | "Guard your steps" | Formal English idiom |
| PNEUMA | "keep your ears open and your mouth shut" | Interpretive paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Guard your steps" (LOGOS). The singular "foot" functions as a Hebrew idiom for conduct. "Steps" is natural English.

---

## 5:6 — "the messenger" — identity disputed

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-messenger [ha-mal'akh]" | Literal — ambiguous referent |
| LOGOS | "the messenger" | Preserves ambiguity |
| PNEUMA | "God's messenger" | Specifies divine origin |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the messenger" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew *ha-mal'akh* is ambiguous and should remain so.

---

## 5:7 — "vanity/vapor" vs. "talk is cheap"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "vanities [hevelim] and-many words" | Literal plural of hevel |
| LOGOS | "there is vanity" | Formal summary |
| PNEUMA | "Talk is cheap, like so many dreams" | Dynamic paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "there is vapor" — maintaining the consensus *hevel* rendering. PNEUMA's "talk is cheap" imports a modern idiom.

**Status:** All resolved.
